children: The outlook for the euro-dollar exchange rate could remain challenging until lofty U.S. interest-rate rise expectations are called into question, Commerzbank's Michael Pfister says in a note. U.S. core inflation unexpectedly remained at 0.3% month-on-month in October, the level at which Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-points rate increase should be considered in December. Such a move seems unlikely but his comments highlight a shift toward considering more aggressive tightening, Pfister says. The euro has the disadvantage of inflation expectations being more closely linked to oil prices, which have eased, while the European Central Bank started tightening earlier so is unlikely to follow suit with the same vigor, he says. The euro falls 0.1% to $1.1155. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
